rows.what_the_ink_shows: In the final line, the first g has a short single subscript stroke, reading g_1, and the relation continues =20c_1. The second coefficient is also 20: the last digit is a single open oval, unlike the two-lobed 8 in the earlier relations. The subscript at the second g merges into its descending stroke, and the final c subscript is a narrow descending hook; their shapes do not securely settle 2 versus 3. The existing in-place uncertainties are therefore retained. Directly inspected crops/62_scan091_L832_final_relations.png, plus same-page numeral comparisons in crops/62_scan091_L832_boxed_comparison.png and crops/62_scan091_L832_middle_comparison.png after the full scan. The comparison relations visibly read g_2=20c_1 and g_3=28c_2.
rows.note: For the cote 62 / scan 91 portion of L832, the final line is preserved as $g_1=20c_1$, $g_{\unsure{2|3}}=20c_{\unsure{3|2}}$. The supplied intended relations g_2=20c_1 and g_3=28c_2 occur clearly earlier on this same page, but the final line visibly differs in the first g subscript and the second coefficient. Applying those intended relations here would correct author slips rather than transcribe the final-line ink. Both existing subscript uncertainties remain in place. The scan 62 and scan 80 portions of the compound row were not adjudicated in this review; no mathematical proof is claimed.
rows.main_resolution: Main reader inspected the final-line crop and both same-page comparison crops. The first g subscript is a short 1 and the second coefficient is 20, while the final g and c indices remain too compressed to choose 2 or 3 reliably. Retain both existing in-place uncertainty macros; this resolves the editorial action without claiming the ink itself is settled.
